note: River access, timber and fields on an unchannelized stretch of the upper Grand River south of Albany. The area map marks primitive camping at three gravel lots in woods along the gravel road in from 430th Street on the north side (this pin is the easternmost, near the river bend), and a fourth by the boat ramp at the Old Havana Trail bridge. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: area page 'Individual Campsites'; brochure 'Primitive camping is permitted only in areas identified on area map', 14 days in 30; map (02/13) shows 4 Primitive Camping Area symbols, GIS 244-247. Free/FCFS/no hookups/14 nights written manual. Pin (GIS 244) fine. No split: the only separately reached camp (247) is at the boat-ramp lot. Not waterfront kept. Phone matches.
flags: INCLUSION/FIT: area page 'Camping: Individual Campsites'. Brochure: 'Primitive camping is permitted only in areas identified on area map. Camping is limited to 14 consecutive days in a 30-day period... campers or more must obtain a special use permit.' The map marks four 'Primitive Camping Area' symbols, each by a parking lot: three along the north gravel road (in from 430th Street) and one at the Old Havana Trail boat ramp with a privy and accessible symbol. Imagery: the pin camp is a ~25 x 40 m gravel lot in woods at the east end of the north road; camps 245/246 are similar gravel lots ~0.8-0.9 km W on the same road. A 23-ft rig fits each. No ford/4WD/rig wording.

CLUSTERS: 245 40.0913,-94.2677 and 246 40.0908,-94.2666 (0.8-0.9 km W, same north road and entrance - no split); 247 40.0757,-94.2538 (1.76 km S, reached by Old Havana Trail from Route Z/McFall, a different road and entrance).

NO SPLIT for 247: the map's camping symbol there sits with the boat ramp, its lot and privy; on imagery the GIS point is in the trees ~40 m SE of the east end of the gravel boat-ramp lot with no pad or lane visible, so vehicle camping there is in effect the ramp lot. That is the lot-allowance pattern the brief says not to add; reported, not split. If AWH reads the mapped symbol as a designated area beside the lot (as at Dupont), a split 'Elam Bend Conservation Area (Old Havana Trail camp)' at 40.0760,-94.2546 (lot 56) would be the candidate; the Grand River is ~40 m N of that lot across the ramp lane and bank trees.

WATERFRONT (not waterfront, kept): the map draws the Grand River bend just north of the pin's lot, but on imagery there is no water within the 155 m frame around the pin - the lot is enclosed by woods and fields, the river 80 m+ away through trees.
Note rewritten: acreage, generic MDC text, the 14-day limit (now booking.max_stay_nights) and directions dropped; where the camps are put in.
